claim: The dctta notebook writes a self-reported integrity receipt declaring no metric hack and no use of organizer labels, consistent with the code actually read.
The dctta notebook writes a runtime integrity receipt asserting ground truth was never accessed during inference.
The 0.947 family does no training in the notebook: all five attach the same three pilkwang datasets and only run inference.
The only script the notebook ever executes is predict_unet_transformer.py; train_unet_transformer.py appears only as a SHA256 integrity entry, never invoked.
Primary weights are a pretrained UNet+transformer checkpoint shipped in the support pack, 8.3 MB, config 32/64/128 U-Net with window_size 2 and downsample (1,4,4).
A second, independently seeded copy of the same architecture is attached as the secondary model for a dual-seed ensemble.
A third pretrained model, the DeepCenter full-frame-center detector, is loaded purely as a veto/confirmation prior.
Voxel scale is anisotropic 1.625 x 0.40625 x 0.40625 um; the (1,4,4) downsample makes the working grid isotropic at 1.625 um.
The detector is learned, not classical: a 3D+T U-Net with per-voxel multi-head self-attention across time, channels 32/64/128.
The detection head is a single 1x1x1 Conv3d producing one logit channel from the 32-channel U-Net features.
Detection targets are single hard voxels, not Gaussian blobs - no sigma, no radius.
Detection loss is BCEWithLogits with a per-sample positive/negative reweighting map, negatives scaled by det_neg_weight=1e-2.

claim: Edge loss is a softmax over the SOURCE axis plus focal-modulated BCE with gamma=2; dim=0 is deliberate so divisions are allowed but merges are not.
quote:
probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=0)  # dim=0 intentional: divisions allowed, merges aren't
    bce = F.binary_cross_entropy(probs, target, reduction="none")
    p_t = probs * target + (1 - probs) * (1 - target)
    loss = ((1 - p_t) ** 2) * bce

claim: The linker is a learned pairwise scorer, not nearest neighbour: a bidirectional cross-attention transformer over node features that emits a dense N_t x N_t1 logit matrix.
Edge candidates are ALL pairs between consecutive frames - there is no linking radius at the scoring stage, only a probability threshold.
Greedy acceptance is capped at 1 parent and 2 children per node only when the ILP is disabled; with ILP on, the caps are left unconstrained.
Global linking is a tracksdata ILP solver over edge probability with appearance, disappearance and division costs.
The dctta family runs the ILP with zero appearance cost and disappearance cost 2 - free to start tracks, expensive to end them (division cost is set to 1.2 at line 44).
CRITICAL: after the ILP, the notebook DISCARDS every ILP edge and replaces them wholesale with its own motion-relink assignment.
The real linker is a two-pass Hungarian assignment with a constant-velocity motion prediction, gated at 6.0 um (tight) then 10.0 um (relaxed) - which brackets the ~8.4 um effective radius.

claim: Edge-feature TTA is explicitly switched on for the primary model.
The secondary model's edge-feature TTA is blended only partially - 0.75 of the TTA-averaged features, 0.25 of the single-pass features.
The only difference between biohub-lf-dctta (0.947) and biohub-lf-dctta025-sectta1 (0.947) is the secondary edge-feature TTA weight, 0.75 vs 1.0 - both score the same.
Edge TTA here averages FEATURES, not predictions or graphs - which is why it helps where naive edge/graph-level TTA hurts.
The edge model is run in BOTH time directions and the two are fused by a weighted harmonic mean in probability space, requiring mutual forward/reverse support.
Before fusion the reverse-time logits are mean/std recalibrated onto the forward logit scale, ratio clamped to [0.5, 2.0].
The reverse-time association weight is 0.15 and the fusion mode is harmonic_probability; the config guard hard-fails if either drifts.

A second independently-seeded model blends into the edge logits at weight 0.15 using low_margin_consensus, which applies the secondary only where the primary is uncertain AND the two agree on the top parent.
In low_margin_consensus mode the secondary weight scales with primary uncertainty and is zeroed whenever the two models disagree on the best parent.

claim: Minimum track length is 6 nodes, and components containing a division are exempt from that filter.
Isolated nodes are pruned and single-parent repair is on, but single-child repair is deliberately off so divisions survive.
Gap closing spans up to 2 frames at 5.0 um, with a density-adaptive radius that widens in sparse neighbourhoods by gain 0.040 per um, capped at 0.125 um per step.
Gap closure reuses an existing node within 3.2 um before inserting a synthetic one, and synthetic midpoints are snapped to a local intensity maximum within 3.2 um.
Newly inserted gap nodes are capped at 5 percent of the graph or 2000 nodes, whichever is smaller.
Every synthetic gap node is confirmed by the DeepCenter heatmap at threshold 0.25, and only for gaps spanning at least 8.5 um.
Short tracks below length 6 can be rescued back if their mean edge probability exceeds 0.88 and mean edge length is under 3.0 um, capped at 1.2 percent of nodes or 120 nodes.
Node coordinates are smoothed by a local line fit with weight 0.8 over a window of 2 frames as the final step.
The DeepCenter veto model is a separate 3-level 3D U-Net with conv-GN-SiLU blocks and 24 base channels, pooling only XY by 4 so Z stays full resolution.

claim: The five 0.947 notebooks are the same 4200-line file; sjlee101/biohub-lf-dctta-v020 differs from biohub-lf-dctta by exactly one environment variable, the DeepCenter safe-division threshold (0.20 vs 0.25).
The notebook admits its base is a public 0.939 run and that the gain came from holdout-selected post-processing, not a new model.
The config guard hard-fails the run if any of six tuned constants drift, showing these values were selected, not incidental.
The notebook runs its own offline replica of the official metric and a post-process sweep, accepting a config only if it gains more than 0.001 and loses less than 0.0005 adjusted edge jaccard.
The local validator matches nodes bipartitely at a 7.0 um radius with node-count penalty 0.1 and division weight 0.1, mirroring the competition metric.
Inference is sharded across visible GPUs as parallel subprocesses, which is how a dual-model 8-view-TTA bidirectional run fits in ~110 minutes.
The pilkwang two-seeds notebook, an ancestor of this family, uses a stricter detection threshold 0.96875 and disables gap2 recovery - the honest-baseline variant of the same code.
Detection logits are also fused across the two seeds, with the secondary weighted 0.80 - the secondary seed dominates DETECTION while contributing only 0.15 to linking.
A retention guard reverts a frame to primary-only detection whenever the dual-seed blend retains under 90 percent of the primary's candidate peaks, so the ensemble can never cost node recall.

claim: The minimum candidate retention is 0.90 and is one of the six constants the config guard refuses to let drift.
The bidirectional harmonic fusion runs BEFORE the dual-seed secondary blend, so the secondary is calibrated against already-fused forward logits.
The notebook prints a reverse-time association weight of 0.200 while the guarded value actually in force is 0.15 - a stale print string, not a functional bug.
The dual-seed edge candidate threshold of 0.48 overrides the repo default only when a secondary model is actually loaded.

CAVEAT: the notebook self-declares that leaderboard feedback WAS used to choose its configuration, so 0.947 is a public-LB-tuned number and the post-process constants carry overfitting risk on the private split.
The post-process sweep is selected on a small internal validator (4 samples per type), which is a thin basis for the constants it picks.
